videos.script: boxoffice charges money for every order. It does that by calling a payment provider. {{dependency}} In a test you cannot use the real one. It costs money, you cannot make it fail when you want, and it is not yours. So you put something in its place. A small program that answers the way the provider would. {{stand-in}} First you write one yourself, in Node. It approves, declines, or answers too late, whichever you ask for. And it remembers what boxoffice sent it. {{stub}} Then WireMock, a tool built for this. You describe each answer in a file, and it tells you when a request matched nothing. {{wiremock}} Then Prism. It reads the contract from lesson 2 and answers from it, before the real API even exists. {{prism}} And then the hard part. A stand-in is a claim about another program, and claims go stale. {{lie}} You will watch a mock answer 200 where the provider answers 201, and catch it with the provider's own contract. {{catch}} By the end you can replace a dependency, and tell when the replacement has stopped telling the truth.
